title_vi: Thanh toán ngoại tệ: 100 đô la thành 88 euro

claims.claim_vi: Example: the buyer pays in USD and the European seller receives euros; this process is called foreign exchange. Bob (buyer) pays 100 USD to Alice (seller), who can only receive EUR.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Step 1: Bob sends 100 USD via a third-party payment provider, PayPal; the money moves from Bob's bank account (Bank B) to PayPal's account in Bank P1.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Steps 2 to 4: PayPal uses the foreign exchange provider (Bank E); PayPal sends 100 USD to its USD account in Bank E; the 100 USD is sold to Bank E's funding pool; the pool gives 88 EUR in exchange, put into PayPal's EUR account in Bank E.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: Steps 5 and 6: PayPal's EUR account in Bank P2 receives 88 EUR; 88 EUR is paid to Alice's EUR account in Bank A.
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: The forex market has three layers: the retail market (funding pools are part of it; to be efficient PayPal usually buys some foreign currency in advance), the wholesale market (investment banks, commercial banks, foreign exchange providers; usually handles accumulated orders from the retail market) and top-level participants (multinational commercial banks holding lots of money from different countries).
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: When Bank E's funding pool needs more EUR it goes to the wholesale market to sell USD and buy EUR; when the wholesale market accumulates enough orders it goes to the top-level participants (steps 3.1 to 3.3 and 4.1 to 4.3).
claims.verified_by: Source body read at the pinned commit.

claims.claim_vi: That 88 for 100 implies a rate of 0.88 euro per dollar in this example only is the author's arithmetic; the source does not state a rate.
claims.verified_by: Author's general knowledge; not checked against payment-industry documentation.

design_notes_vi: Hai khung ba bước đánh số cho đường đi của tiền (thứ tự quan trọng, chia đôi ở chỗ đô la đã bán xong và euro bắt đầu về), rồi một khung ba tầng của thị trường ngoại hối nối bằng mũi tên đi lên, đúng chiều quỹ tiền đi tìm thêm euro. Ba chữ "ngân hàng B, P1, P2, E, A" giữ như nguồn để người đọc đối chiếu với hình gốc.
source_deviations: The source writes USD and EUR; the lesson writes "đô la" and "euro" to avoid abbreviations that need a glossary.
The source explains the upward route with sub-steps 3.1 to 3.3 and 4.1 to 4.3 shown in the diagram; the lesson keeps only the written rule (go up when more currency is needed).
The source gives 88 EUR for 100 USD as an example; the lesson keeps it as an example and states no rate.
